knowledge_gaps: The gate weakly suppresses incoherent windows: for five normalized embeddings, mean off-diagonal cosine is at least -1/4, so g is at least 0.375. Orthogonal embeddings and singleton histories both receive g=0.5. The report does not justify this mapping.

Coherence and pooled-vector magnitude are coupled: for n unit embeddings, ||mean(E)||² = [1+(n-1)c]/n. Gating may merely reinforce attenuation already produced by averaging. Learned embedding geometry can also optimize the gate without representing meaningful coherence; negative alpha further complicates the interpretation.

Reproduction requires specifying raw versus normalized pooling embeddings, embedding scaling and dropout, placement relative to final normalization, gradient flow through the gate, scalar scope per dataset, and final valid-position extraction. Diagnostic decomposition must subtract the complete gated branch.

The comparison lacks an explicit compute allocation, checkpoint-selection rule, and scale-matched constant-gate control. Fixed seeds alone do not guarantee matched backbone initialization and training randomness. Adaptive validation selection remains a risk.

Originality 5/10 and potential 7/10 are provisional without directly related gated short-term recommendation baselines or empirical gains. Difficulty 3/10 assumes vectorized causal pooling and verified training–predictor–diagnosis parity. Supplied references remain unverified.
